text:
MyDB

 A high-performance MySQL-compatible database for HTAP and AI agents 

Mixed transactional and analytical workloads, with native AI retrieval.

English · 简体中文

Download · Why MyDB · Performance evaluation · Testing · Quick Start · Built for AI Agents · Documentation · MySQL Compatibility

 

---

MyDB is a general-purpose database built in Rust for HTAP (hybrid
transactional/analytical processing), AI agents, and MySQL compatibility .
It is designed for mixed workloads that combine transactional reads and writes
with analytical queries over the same business data. Native full-text and
vector retrieval and external model calls extend these workflows through
familiar SQL.

Applications can reuse MySQL clients and drivers, while native REST and MCP
interfaces give services and agents direct access to the same engine. Automatic
Zone Maps, online schema changes, and directly queryable backups reduce the
work needed to tune access, evolve data structures, and inspect earlier data.

MyDB 1.0.3 is a public-preview release intended for feature validation and controlled-environment evaluation.
See the 1.0.3 release notes for changes and upgrade requirements.

 Core advantage What it gives you 
 --- --- 
 Built for AI agents Native vectors, hybrid retrieval, SQL model calls, and REST/MCP access connect agents with business data. 
 High-performance HTAP Transactional reads and writes alongside analytical queries on one dataset, with parallel execution, vectorization, and automatic Zone Maps. 
 MySQL compatible Reuse MySQL clients, JDBC drivers, common SQL, and ROW/FULL binlog integration. 

Read Why MyDB for the application benefits, design choices,
and published evidence behind these advantages. RRF is a technical preview;
the linked references describe each capability's supported scope.

 Performance evaluation

 Over 1 million QPS on 16 CPU cores — sysbench, November 16, 2026:

 Workload MyDB QPS P95 latency 
 --- ---: ---: 
 oltp point select 1,327,407.37 0.55 ms 

The November 16, 2026 MyDB snapshot ran on a 16-core CPU VM, with 100M rows
across 10 tables, 300 client threads on a separate host over the private network, and one
300-second run using sysbench's special access distribution. No errors or
reconnects were recorded. See the full benchmark report
for configuration, methodology, and complete results.

 Smart indexing: fewer full scans without manual indexes

Changing filters and agent-generated SQL make query patterns hard to predict.
MyDB enables automatic Zone Maps on persistent user tables by default.
Per-block summaries let eligible scans skip blocks that cannot match a
predicate, reducing work without requiring a hand-built B-tree index for every
filtering pattern. Serial, parallel, and vectorized scans retain final
predicate checks; missing or untrusted summaries fall back to a regular scan.

On 15 million TPC-H SF=10 orders , with no user-created indexes in either
database, MyDB 1.0.3 and MySQL 8.0.46 produced these lookup results:

 Lookup MyDB median (ms) MySQL median (ms) Speedup 
 --- ---: ---: ---: 
 Order ID (ordered column) 1.206 7,577.824 6,281.8x 
 Customer ID (scattered column) 32.466 7,678.232 236.5x 

Single-threaded, warm-cache medians cover five random values with three
executions per value; speedup is MySQL time / MyDB time. See the
no-index lookup benchmark for the schema,
SQL, scanned pages, disk space, and full test conditions.

The benefit depends on data layout and selectivity. See the
feature overview for the mechanism and fallbacks.

 MyDB vs. MySQL 8.0 , measured November 17, 2026:

 Workload MyDB MySQL Advantage 
 --- --- --- --- 
 Point queries · 100M rows, 20 clients 295,724 queries/s 184,108 queries/s 1.61x throughput 
 Read-only transactions · 100M rows, 20 clients 13,522 transactions/s 7,477 transactions/s 1.81x throughput 
 TPC-H-derived analytics · SF=10, 22 query medians summed 50.636 s 1,205.299 s 23.80x speedup 
 TPC-DS-derived analytics · SF=10, 84/99 matching on MyDB and MySQL 92.427 s 4,468.101 s 48.34x speedup on that subset 
 Bulk import · TPC-H SF=10, LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE 37.281 s 374.490 s 10.04x speedup 

Same 16-vCPU host, 10 GiB database memory limits, and durable commits.
TPC-DS reports only matching MyDB/MySQL files; its subset differs from the
historical three-engine subset. TPC-derived results are unaudited. See the
detailed comparison for results, test
conditions, result differences, and limitations.

 Cohere 1M HNSW , November 24, 2026: 768-dimensional FLOAT32 cosine Top-100,
with MyDB query-candidate memoization disabled.

 Database memory limit MyDB, 16 clients PostgreSQL 18.6 + pgvector 0.8.7 MyDB throughput 
 --- ---: ---: ---: 
 32 GiB 5,121 queries/s 2,142 queries/s 2.39x 
 2 GiB 458 queries/s 139 queries/s 3.29x 

Both engines used the same 16-vCPU host and durable commits. At 32 GiB,
Recall@100 was 94.741% vs 94.395%; at 2 GiB it was
95.331% vs 94.341%. See the
Cohere 1M benchmark for index-build times,
latency, settings, and all query rounds.

 Testing

 Over 12,000 automated regression tests and one million fuzz input executions. 
The main and Safety CI runs below are from November 17, 2026, at commit
 1316cbf4 .

 Test area Verified scope and results Evidence

 Automated regressions 12,077 passed across three test partitions. CI 
 SQL functions 450 function names , including aliases, have associated tests; 430 names have 1,294 fixture cases , with dedicated integration tests for the other 20. CI

 Concurrency and fault recovery 4 Jepsen workloads, 8 crash/COMMIT-disconnect recovery cases and 16 I/O fault combinations passed , alongside native replication and semi-sync checks. Safety CI

install.title: Quick Start
install.html:
Download prebuilt packages for macOS ARM64, Linux x86_64, and Windows x64 from the 1.0.3 release page, which also includes SHA256 checksums and platform validation details.

Run a downloaded binary

Download the package for your platform, extract it, and open a terminal in the directory containing the executable. On macOS or Linux, start it with:

chmod +x ./mydb
./mydb --data-dir ./data

On Windows, run the equivalent command in PowerShell:

.\mydb.exe --data-dir ./data

The server listens on all IPv4 interfaces (0.0.0.0:8738) and stores data in ./data. No Rust toolchain or config file is needed. With a MySQL 8.0 client installed, connect from another terminal:

mysql -h127.0.0.1 -P8738 -uroot -proot test

A fresh data directory includes the test database and the local root account with password root. Run SELECT 1; to check the connection. Enter quit to exit the client, then press Ctrl+C in the server terminal to stop it. Restart with the same data directory to reopen your data.

Native Rust client

Build the independent client from a source checkout:

cargo build --release --locked --manifest-path clients/mydb-cli/Cargo.toml
./clients/mydb-cli/target/release/mydb-cli -h127.0.0.1 -P8738 -uroot -p test

The client provides interactive editing and completion, SQL scripts, table/TSV/ vertical output, TLS, and query cancellation. See the client manual.

Build and connect

Install Rust 1.95 or newer, a native C toolchain, Perl, and a MySQL 8.0 client; the shell commands below target macOS and Linux.

git clone https://github.com/yzsind/mydb.git
cd mydb
cargo build --release --locked --bin mydb

MYDB_DATA_DIR=/tmp/mydb/data \
  ./target/release/mydb --port 8738

When the server is ready, connect from another terminal:

mysql -h127.0.0.1 -P8738 -uroot -proot test

A fresh data directory creates root@localhost with password root and a test database. This account accepts only loopback connections. MYDB_ROOT_PASSWORD sets the initial password on first start; it does not change existing accounts. The default protocol port is 8738; override it with --port.

Try a write, an aggregate, and a window function:

CREATE TABLE orders (
    id BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,
    region VARCHAR(32),
    amount DECIMAL(12, 2)
);

INSERT INTO orders VALUES
    (1, 'east', 120.00),
    (2, 'south', 80.00),
    (3, 'east', 180.00);

SELECT region,
       SUM(amount) AS revenue,
       DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY SUM(amount) DESC) AS revenue_rank
FROM orders
GROUP BY region
ORDER BY revenue_rank, region;
Docker

Pull the prebuilt image from Docker Hub and run a container (stop any local instance using port 8738 first):

docker pull ninedata/mydb:latest
docker volume create mydb-data

docker run -d --name mydb \
  -p 127.0.0.1:8738:8738 \
  -v mydb-data:/var/lib/mydb \
  -e MYDB_ROOT_PASSWORD='change-me' \
  ninedata/mydb:latest

docker exec -it mydb mysql -h127.0.0.1 -P8738 -uroot -p --ssl

Enter change-me for the password on a fresh volume. Stop with docker stop mydb and restart with docker start mydb; the named volume retains the data. Bridge/NAT connections through the published port do not match root@localhost — create a dedicated account in that SQL session for host connections. The image enables TLS, fast-alloc, and the MySQL replication receiver by default. See the Docker deployment guide for certificates, mounted configuration, cross-architecture builds, and connecting from the host.

Platforms and distribution

Supported operating systems: macOS (arm64 and Intel) and Linux (x86_64 and aarch64), plus Windows 11 for foreground operation on local NTFS. See hardware and OS requirements for verification details, Windows limitations, and distribution scope.
